correctness.rationale: For any finite simple F with n≥1, each pendant leaf ℓ_v forces every dominating set to meet the disjoint pair {v,ℓ_v}; selecting all originals dominates B(F), hence γ(B(F))=n. Equality chooses exactly one per pair and excludes every subdivision vertex. A subdivider w_uv is dominated precisely when at least one endpoint u,v rather than its leaf is chosen: therefore selected-leaf indices form an independent set I, and every I yields exactly D(I). Consequently the marked polynomial is I_F(t). Any size-preserving swap between min sets must flip the same pair v↔ℓ_v, an actual edge, giving identical token-slide and unrestricted exchange reconfiguration graphs, the simplex graph S(complement F). Removing I\J then adding J\I gives exact Hamming metric; the majority of three independent sets is independent, giving medianity. Every k-dimensional induced cube in the ambient coordinate hypercube is a coordinate face with a unique maximum independent set I and k freely toggled positions: c_k=Σ_I binom(|I|,k), so C(q)=I_F(1+q). Direct degrees, subdivision cycles, leaf attachments establish size 2n+|E|, bipartiteness, girth at least six, maximum degree max{Δ+1,2}, planarity and connectivity claims. Cubic independent-set #P-hardness transfers parsimoniously to the specified degree-four bipartite high-girth family; no unproved general #P-membership claim. Inspected source verifier tests 1,369,076 subsets across 81 graphs, and independently developed checker additionally exhausts 78 graphs including all n≤4, compares real minimum-set adjacencies, BFS distances and cube counts. These finite tests substantiate but do not replace unrestricted combinatorial proof. Edge cases n=1, isolated vertices, empty E and disconnected F are included.

Xie–Feng–Xu 2024 proves C(G,q)=Cl(G#,1+q) for every median graph and realizes any graph as the crossing graph of a simplex graph, thereby ALREADY implying C(S(complement F),q)=I_F(1+q). The standalone simplex-graph cube identity is prior, not new.

value.rationale: The all-source, explicit restricted realization transfers complete minimum dominating-set families, marked solution-size polynomial, exact token-slide/jump metric, and a parsimonious cubic-input counting reduction into a sparse bipartite host of girth≥6. These constraints matter for domination reconfiguration and counting and are not implied by unconstrained family realization. Although private-pair arguments and the cube identity once the simplex graph is identified are elementary/previously known, the uniform solution-family representation across arbitrary source graphs is a motivated structural result rather than arbitrary unmotivated sampling. Value is limited to this specified known graph operation; it does not extend to all bipartite graphs and does not make old median/cube facts new.
